method.value: 2D PLUTO simulations of a vortex triggered at an MRI dead-zone inner edge and of a vortex at the edge of a gap opened by a 1 Jupiter-mass planet

key_parameters.value: LINEAR reconstruction, 2nd order Runge-Kutta, HLLC solver, viscosity via Super-Time-Stepping, CFL 0.4

evidence.quote: We use a PLUTO numerical setup with LINEAR reconstruction method, 2nd order Runge-Kutta time-stepping, the Harten-Lax-Van Leer Riemann (HLLC) solver
We set the Courant number (CFL) to 0.4.

key_parameters.value: Domain 0.3-3.0 code units radially and 2 pi in azimuth; 1024 x 2048 cells (r, phi), uniform spacing

evidence.quote: The simulation domain covers 0.3-3.0 code units of length in the radial direction, and $2 \pi$ rad in azimuth.

key_parameters.value: alpha_DZ = 1e-5, alpha_0 = 1e-3, r_DZ = 1.2 r_0, Delta_DZ = H(r_DZ)

key_parameters.value: Planet case: 1 M_J planet at r_p = r_0, smoothing length 60% of local scale height, mass taper over 30 orbits, constant alpha = 1e-5

evidence.quote: In a second setup, we include a $1\,M_{\mathrm{J}}$ planet
a potential smoothing length set to $60\%$ of the local disk pressure scale height

evidence.quote: We have used a scaling radius of 70 au to convert from code units to physical units
The simulation snapshots depicted correspond to 400 orbits measured at 1 code unit of length (dead zone) and 580 planetary orbits, respectively.
We consider a two-dimensional disk in polar coordinates, including the evolution of the gas only.

assumptions.value: Locally isothermal equation of state, H/r = 0.05 at r_0, sound speed proportional to r^-0.25, flared disk H proportional to r^1.25

evidence.quote: Our simulations follow a locally isothermal equation of state $P=c_{\mathrm{s}}^2 \Sigma$

The effects of disk self-gravity are not taken into account in our models.

findings_qualitative.value: None of the four disks shows a distinctive vortex kinematic signature around the dust crescents

evidence.quote: we find that none of the sources show a distinctive vortex signature around the dust crescents in the kinematics.

findings_qualitative.value: HD 135344B shows a feature similar to the simulation predictions and is the most promising target for follow-up

evidence.quote: HD 135344B exhibits a prominent feature similar to the predictions from the simulations, thus making this the most promising target for sensitive follow-up studies

findings_qualitative.value: Including a planet adds its own Doppler flip and much stronger spirals that mask the vortex pattern

evidence.quote: If a planet is included in the disk, it creates its own Doppler-flip signature and much stronger spiral features, which overlay on the pattern associated with the vortex, thus making it much harder to distinguish.

findings_qualitative.value: Inner velocity-residual spirals align somewhat with NIR spirals in HD 135344B and MWC 758

evidence.quote: For both disks, the inner spirals seen in the velocity residuals appear to align somewhat with the NIR spirals.

findings_qualitative.value: Dust asymmetries are about the size of the beam, so vortex signatures may be unresolved

evidence.quote: it becomes clear that they are very similar, thus the vortex signatures may not be resolved and therefore do not clearly show up in the kinematics.

claims.hypothesis: The dust crescents in four exoALMA disks are accompanied by a vortex kinematic signature in 12CO and 13CO
claims.experiment: Compared 12CO and 13CO velocity residuals with mock residuals of a dead-zone vortex simulation, with dust contours overlaid
claims.result: Most disks show no clear vortex signature; HD 135344B has a red-blue pattern shifted from the dust asymmetry and overlaid by spirals
claims.finding: None of the sources shows a distinctive vortex signature; HD 135344B is the most convincing case

evidence.quote: we find that none of the sources show a distinctive vortex signature around the dust crescents in the kinematics.
Among our sample, this makes HD 135344B the most convincing example of a vortex and the best target to pursue with even deeper observations at very high angular resolution.

claims.hypothesis: A simple 2D analytical vortex model can constrain the vortex properties of the dust crescents by fitting the residuals
claims.experiment: Implemented the analytical model in eddy and fitted different disk regions
claims.result: None of the runs converged and the distributions were very degenerate
claims.finding: A simple model is not sufficient to constrain vortex properties

evidence.quote: However, none of these runs converged and resulted in very degenerate distributions.
we conclude that a simple model is not sufficient to constrain the properties of the vortex

claims.hypothesis: A vortex gives a recognisable red-blue kinematic pattern, and an embedded planet confuses it
claims.experiment: Analytical model and 2D PLUTO simulations of a dead-zone vortex and a vortex at a planet gap edge
claims.result: Both show a red-blue dipole plus spirals; the planet adds its own Doppler flip and much stronger spirals
claims.finding: The planetary scenario makes the vortex signature much harder to distinguish

evidence.quote: If a planet is included in the disk, it creates its own Doppler-flip signature and much stronger spiral features, which overlay on the pattern associated with the vortex, thus making it much harder to distinguish.

claims.hypothesis: Spiral features in the gas residuals of HD 135344B and MWC 758 trace the NIR scattered-light spirals
claims.experiment: Compared polar-deprojected CO residuals with NIR scattered-light spirals
claims.result: Inner velocity spirals align somewhat with NIR spirals; peak intensity aligns well for MWC 758 but not HD 135344B
claims.finding: Partial alignment between gas residual and NIR spirals

evidence.quote: For both disks, the inner spirals seen in the velocity residuals appear to align somewhat with the NIR spirals.

why_this_data.value: The four disks are among the six most asymmetric exoALMA disks in continuum and show evidence of azimuthal dust traps

evidence.quote: They are among the six most asymmetric disks in continuum (cite: Curone_exoALMA) in the exoALMA sample and all show evidence of azimuthal dust traps in their millimetre (mm) continuum

why_this_method.value: A dead-zone edge is used to trigger the vortex at a chosen location, so the dead-zone and planet cases can be compared

evidence.quote: we set up the simulation in this way to trigger a vortex at a particular location
creating a vortex in the same location for both the dead zone and embedded planet simulation makes it easier to compare the two cases

limitations_admitted.value: Predictions rely on 2D models; vertical motions are not captured

evidence.quote: The vortex predictions presented in this work rely on 2D models.

limitations_admitted.value: Results may be limited by spatial resolution relative to the dust asymmetries

evidence.quote: our results may also limited be by the spatial resolution in comparison to the size of the dust asymmetries

limitations_admitted.value: Low inclination of three of four sources makes azimuthal motions hard to detect

referee_caveats_inferred: The comparison between data and simulation is visual, with no quantitative metric or significance test
Only one vortex model (dead-zone edge) was convolved and compared; vortex properties were not varied to fit each source
Inferring a vortex from residuals depends on the DISCMINER Keplerian subtraction in companion papers, so residual artefacts could mimic or hide a signal
12CO and 13CO trace upper layers, which the 2D midplane-like model does not represent

missing_for_reproduction: Fiducial exoALMA cubes and DISCMINER residual maps are produced in companion papers (Teague, Loomis, Izquierdo, Fukagawa)
Vortex placement and strength per source in the mock images
RADMC-3D thermal and chemical set-up for the mock CO cubes
No code or simulation outputs stated as released
Data release status of the exoALMA images is not stated in this paper
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Several GB to tens of GB: fiducial exoALMA 12CO and 13CO cubes for four disks (raw measurement sets would be much larger)
reproducibility.score_reason: The ALMA project code is printed, but the imaging, DISCMINER residuals and extraction are in companion papers. The simulation setup is mostly given, but the mock-image setup is incomplete, there is no released code, and the main conclusion is a qualitative visual comparison.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The key products come from other papers, the mock radiative transfer set-up is incomplete, and the main result is qualitative rather than numeric.
